title: How he wants the Workshop remembered
summary: He wants it remembered for artists' sacrifice and as a seed of current New Orleans music, urging the city to nurture young talent.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Okay. How do you want the workshop remembered?

I want the workshop remembered as a place for people to become cognizant of just the kind of sacrifice and dedication that musicians and all artists put into their work, uh, so that they can bring a part of themselves and a part of their experience in sharing themselves with people. Uh, to be remembered as a place that some of new, the seeds and the foundation of some of the greatest New Orleans music that you hear now and that you've heard in the past few years that what we at the workshop and all of those volunteers and all those people that came together to make happen, uh, what kind of impact that had on what you're hearing now and without it, I don't think we, we would have quite as rich of a musical environment as we have as a result of what, what we put into that workshop and, uh, hopefully something that will make the, the people that turn the wheels that operate the, the city and all its various institutions to recognize that never again can we allow ourselves to be negligent of not reaching out and developing all of the fresh talents that are in its raw and formative stages to try to do everything we can to give them the right guidance, the right instructors, and the right environment to develop in and hopefully that we, we know that, uh, the music is, is a very serious art form, it's, uh, America's greatest art form in, in my evaluation and many, many others of, of the giants and masters that I've met.
